2026-09-08T12:39:24.7967830Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7968253Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7968840Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7969847Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7970346Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7970903Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7972617Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7974867Z >
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7977957Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7980670Z >
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7981853Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7982723Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7982927Z ### How to Use
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7983188Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7983991Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7984774Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7984981Z ```bash
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7985950Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7986987Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7987666Z ```
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7987896Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7988189Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7988788Z ```bash
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7989737Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7990633Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7991572Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7993387Z ```
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7993668Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7994418Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7995417Z ```bash
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7996053Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7997341Z ```
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7997592Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7997983Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7998843Z ```bash
2026-09-08T12:39:24.7999436Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8000397Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8001538Z ```
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8001779Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8002087Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8002554Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8004103Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8006160Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8006536Z ```bash
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8007061Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8008026Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8009322Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8009705Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8010252Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8011354Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8012586Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8013128Z ```
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8013354Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8014168Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8015467Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8015672Z ```bash
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8016618Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8017965Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8018763Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8019235Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8019976Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8020920Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8021526Z ```
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8021763Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8021994Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8023220Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8024314Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8025702Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8027028Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8028564Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8029171Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8029603Z ### Notes
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8030324Z 
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8031342Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8032920Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8034605Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8035985Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8037940Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8039504Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8040687Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-08T12:39:24.8041473Z </mcp-clis>
